title: API stability policy
text: Versions 0.x.y follow additive--intent evolution. Every minor release (0.x → 0.(x+1)) adds new exports without breaking existing signatures; patch releases fix bugs refresh documentation. Track record far: 0.1.0 — first release (core IES / GLM solvers, SVD backends, surrogates, PEST++ integration, visualisation). 0.1.1 — sole-authorship consolidation; API change. 0.2.0 — added pesto_ies_callback() (-process IES driver) apsim_callback() (apsimx adapter). breaking changes. 0.3.0 — added pesto_ensemble_manifest (S7 cross-package contract) plus as_manifest(), write_manifest(), read_manifest(), verify_manifest(). breaking changes. 0.3.1 — added format = c("rds","","csv") write_manifest(); backwards-compatible YAML. 0.3.2 — renamed format = "csv" "csv_unverified" every call site; legacy "csv" still accepted deprecation warning, 0.3.1 manifests round-trip cleanly. 0.3.3 — Makevars FLIBS portability fix; API change. policy “additive--intent” rather “frozen”: pre-1.0 reserves right break existing signature design flaw surfaces, every change must : Listed ## Breaking changes heading NEWS.md, first. Justified release notes. feasible, accompanied temporary back-compat shim (v0.3.2 csv → csv_unverified rename template: legacy spelling still works deprecation warning). depend PESTO pre-1.0, pin version renv.lock DESCRIPTION (Imports: PESTO (>= 0.3.3)).

title: API stability policy
text: 1.0.0, PESTO adopts strict frozen-API additive evolution — policy glmnet, mgcv, long-lived solver-style packages: Signatures exported functions never change backwards-incompatible way across major versions. New capability arrives via new entry points (new exports), never via changes existing ones. existing function genuinely needs retired, marked lifecycle::deprecate_warn(), kept ≥ 2 minor versions, promoted lifecycle::deprecate_stop() ≥ 1 minor version, removed next major release. Successors signposted deprecation message. policy chosen PESTO invoked IES / surrogate backend pipeline code maintainer edit — kernR consumes pesto_ensemble_manifest S7 contract; APSIM ensemble loops via pesto_ies_callback() written run life calibration campaign. Silent breakage across versions defeat contract.

code: set.seed(20260516L)  npar <- 4L nobs <- 8L nreal <- 120L sigma <- 0.05  G <- matrix(rnorm(nobs * npar), nobs, npar) theta_true <- c(1.0, -0.5, 2.0, 0.25) y <- as.numeric(G %*% theta_true) + rnorm(nobs, sd = sigma) names(y) <- paste0("o", seq_len(nobs))  # Forward model: any function taking an (nreal x npar) matrix and returning # an (nreal x nobs) matrix. forward <- function(theta) theta %*% t(G)  prior <- matrix(rnorm(nreal * npar), nreal, npar,                 dimnames = list(NULL, paste0("p", seq_len(npar)))) fit <- pesto_ies_callback(   forward_model  = forward,   prior_ensemble = prior,   obs            = y,   obs_sd         = sigma,   noptmax        = 6L,   seed           = 42L,   verbose        = FALSE )  prior_rmse <- sqrt(mean((colMeans(prior) - theta_true)^2)) post_mean <- colMeans(as.matrix(fit$par_ensemble[, -1L])) post_rmse <- sqrt(mean((post_mean - theta_true)^2)) round(c(prior_rmse = prior_rmse, posterior_rmse = post_rmse), 4) #>     prior_rmse posterior_rmse  #>         1.1300         0.0231 vec_mean_phi <- vapply(fit$iterations, `[[`, numeric(1L), "mean_phi") round(vec_mean_phi, 3) #> [1] 17452.123    25.006    13.566     9.622     7.592     5.924 tab_phi_wide <- data.table::dcast(   fit$phi, iteration ~ realisation, value.var = "phi" ) plot_phi(tab_phi_wide, show_reals = TRUE,          title = "Misfit by iteration, synthetic recovery problem")

code: fm <- pesto_forward_model(   fn          = forward,   n_obs       = nobs,   param_names = paste0("p", seq_len(npar)),   on_failure  = "na" )  # A contract object is evaluated directly with pesto_evaluate(); the # returned matrix carries the per-realisation failure count. sim <- pesto_evaluate(fm, prior) c(realisations = nrow(sim), outputs = ncol(sim),   failures = attr(sim, "n_failures")) #> realisations      outputs     failures  #>          120            8            0  # Passing the contract to the driver is equivalent to passing the bare # function: the bare form is auto-wrapped internally. fit_typed <- pesto_ies_callback(fm, prior, y, sigma, noptmax = 6L,                                 seed = 42L, verbose = FALSE) identical(   as.matrix(fit_typed$par_ensemble[, -1L]),   as.matrix(fit$par_ensemble[, -1L]) ) #> [1] TRUE

title: Wiring your own simulator into PESTO
text: Process-based crop models expose cost-accuracy dial: daily time step lite soil profile cheap, sub-daily step full profile expensive. pesto_multifidelity_model() makes dial first class. bundles ordered stack fidelity levels, cheapest first, driver picks level per iteration fidelity_schedule, early iterations explore cheaply late ones sharpen expensive truth. final ensemble always refreshed highest fidelity. cheap level run whole ensemble expensive level subset, mf_control_variate() lifts cheap outputs toward expensive ones variance-minimising affine correction, plug-primitive surrogate cascade:
code: # Cheap level: the linear model with a small systematic bias. # Expensive level: the unbiased truth. cheap_fn <- function(theta) theta %*% t(G) + 0.30 expensive_fn <- forward  mf <- pesto_multifidelity_model(   levels = list(     pesto_forward_model(fn = cheap_fn,     n_obs = nobs, fidelity = 0L),     pesto_forward_model(fn = expensive_fn, n_obs = nobs, fidelity = 1L)   ),   costs = c(1, 25)   # the expensive level is about 25 times dearer per run )  # Ramp: two cheap iterations, then four expensive ones. fit_mf <- pesto_ies_callback(   forward_model     = mf,   prior_ensemble    = prior,   obs               = y,   obs_sd            = sigma,   noptmax           = 6L,   fidelity_schedule = c(0L, 0L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L),   seed              = 42L,   verbose           = FALSE )  mf_rmse <- sqrt(mean(   (colMeans(as.matrix(fit_mf$par_ensemble[, -1L])) - theta_true)^2 )) round(c(single_fidelity_rmse = post_rmse, multi_fidelity_rmse = mf_rmse), 4) #> single_fidelity_rmse  multi_fidelity_rmse  #>               0.0231               0.0968 sub <- seq_len(20L) low_all <- pesto_evaluate(mf, prior, level = 0L) low_sub <- low_all[sub, , drop = FALSE] high_sub <- pesto_evaluate(mf, prior[sub, , drop = FALSE], level = 1L)  corrected <- mf_control_variate(low_all, high_sub, low_sub) high_all <- pesto_evaluate(mf, prior, level = 1L) gap_before <- mean(abs(low_all - high_all)) gap_after <- mean(abs(corrected - high_all)) signif(c(mean_gap_before = gap_before, mean_gap_after = gap_after), 3) #> mean_gap_before  mean_gap_after  #>        3.00e-01        3.39e-17

title: Wiring your own simulator into PESTO
text: every simulator sits behind executable. large class, crop growth, epidemic dynamics, nutrient solute transport pharmacokinetics among , small system ordinary differential equations integrated forward time observation vector read state trajectory. PESTO ships templates returning typed contract everything , plug straight driver, multi-fidelity stack manifest emitter. Integration self-contained fixed-step fourth-order Runge-Kutta scheme default, solver = "desolve" path delegating deSolve package stiff systems. generic builder ode_forward_model(): supply derivative function, initial state, time grid, parameter columns model consumes. crop_growth_forward_model() logistic dry-matter curve \mathrm{d}B / \mathrm{d}t = r B (1 - B / b_{\max}), canonical sigmoid description seasonal biomass, calibrating r, b_{\max} starting biomass observed biomass series. Recovery logistic growth parameters noisy biomass series. seir_forward_model() closed-population susceptible-exposed-infectious-recovered epidemic model, calibrating transmission, latency recovery rates observed infectious prevalence curve. reproduction number R_0 = \beta / \gamma summary outbreak curve identifies sharply. templates return pesto_forward_model(), coarse fine fidelity trick previous section applies verbatim: build one template coarse n_steps one fine n_steps, stack pesto_multifidelity_model(), ramp integration resolution across iterations.
code: times <- seq(0, 120, by = 15) crop <- crop_growth_forward_model(times = times)  # Simulate a biomass series at a known parameter, then add field noise. theta_crop <- c(r = 0.06, b_max = 1400, b0 = 20) biomass <- as.numeric(pesto_evaluate(   crop, matrix(theta_crop, nrow = 1L,                dimnames = list(NULL, names(theta_crop))) )) y_crop <- biomass + rnorm(length(biomass), sd = 20) names(y_crop) <- paste0("t", seq_along(y_crop))  prior_crop <- cbind(   r     = runif(120L, 0.02, 0.12),   b_max = runif(120L, 900, 2000),   b0    = runif(120L, 5, 60) ) fit_crop <- pesto_ies_callback(crop, prior_crop, y_crop, obs_sd = 20,                               noptmax = 8L, seed = 42L, verbose = FALSE) post_crop <- colMeans(   as.matrix(fit_crop$par_ensemble[, -1L]) )[names(theta_crop)] days <- seq(0, 60, by = 5) seir <- seir_forward_model(times = days, n_pop = 1000, i0 = 1)  theta_seir <- c(beta = 0.6, sigma = 0.2, gamma = 0.1) prevalence <- as.numeric(pesto_evaluate(   seir, matrix(theta_seir, nrow = 1L,                dimnames = list(NULL, names(theta_seir))) )) y_seir <- prevalence + rnorm(length(prevalence), sd = 3) names(y_seir) <- paste0("d", seq_along(y_seir))  prior_seir <- cbind(   beta  = runif(200L, 0.3, 0.9),   sigma = runif(200L, 0.1, 0.4),   gamma = runif(200L, 0.05, 0.2) ) fit_seir <- pesto_ies_callback(seir, prior_seir, y_seir, obs_sd = 3,                                noptmax = 10L, seed = 42L, verbose = FALSE) post_seir <- colMeans(   as.matrix(fit_seir$par_ensemble[, -1L]) )[names(theta_seir)] r0_truth <- theta_seir[["beta"]] / theta_seir[["gamma"]] r0_post <- post_seir[["beta"]] / post_seir[["gamma"]] round(c(R0_truth = r0_truth, R0_posterior = r0_post), 2) #>     R0_truth R0_posterior  #>         6.00         6.02

code: set.seed(42L)  npar <- 6L nobs <- 10L nreal <- 24L          # a deliberately small ensemble, to provoke collapse  G <- matrix(rnorm(nobs * npar), nobs, npar) theta_true <- rnorm(npar) obs_sd <- 0.3 y <- as.numeric(G %*% theta_true) + rnorm(nobs, sd = obs_sd)  # Analytic posterior standard deviation (standard-normal prior). post_cov <- solve(diag(npar) + crossprod(G) / obs_sd^2) post_sd <- sqrt(diag(post_cov)) round(post_sd, 4) #> [1] 0.1272 0.0826 0.1322 0.1204 0.2000 0.1058  forward <- function(theta) theta %*% t(G) prior <- matrix(rnorm(nreal * npar), nreal, npar,                 dimnames = list(NULL, paste0("p", seq_len(npar)))) run_ies <- function(inflation = NULL, localisation = NULL) {   fit <- pesto_ies_callback(     forward_model  = forward,     prior_ensemble = prior,     obs            = setNames(y, paste0("o", seq_len(nobs))),     obs_sd         = obs_sd,     noptmax        = 12L,     inflation      = inflation,     localisation   = localisation,     seed           = 42L,     verbose        = FALSE   )   par_post <- as.matrix(fit$par_ensemble[, -1L])   last_diag <- fit$iterations[[length(fit$iterations)]]   list(     sd_ratio  = mean(apply(par_post, 2L, sd) / post_sd),     sd_by_par = apply(par_post, 2L, sd) / post_sd,     ess_ratio = last_diag$spread_ess_ratio   ) }

what: Bayesian inference with the Iterative Ensemble Smoother (IES)
title: Parameter Estimation Optimised, with APSIM Coupling
text: PESTO performs approximate Bayesian inference parameter estimation. specify prior parameter ensemble – matrix draws encoding prior belief parameter (rows realisations, columns parameters) – together observations error standard deviation. PESTO conditions ensemble observations IES update returns approximate posterior ensemble uncertainty diagnostics. R function mapping parameter matrix observation matrix can forward model. Optional convergence-based early stopping (phi_tol), covariance inflation (pesto_inflation()), localisation (pesto_localisation()) documented ?pesto_ies_callback Getting started vignette.
code: library(PESTO) set.seed(1)  # Forward model: y = G %*% theta (any R function theta-matrix -> obs-matrix works) G <- matrix(rnorm(6 * 3), 6, 3) forward <- function(theta) theta %*% t(G) truth <- c(a = 1, b = -0.5, c = 2) obs <- stats::setNames(as.numeric(G %*% truth) + rnorm(6, sd = 0.05),                        paste0("o", 1:6))  # Prior: an ensemble of parameter draws (here a broad Gaussian over 3 parameters) prior <- matrix(rnorm(80 * 3), 80, 3, dimnames = list(NULL, names(truth)))  fit <- pesto_ies_callback(forward, prior, obs, obs_sd = 0.05, noptmax = 6,                           verbose = FALSE) colMeans(as.matrix(fit$par_ensemble[, -1]))   # posterior mean -> (1, -0.5, 2) #>          a          b          c  #>  1.0136949 -0.4936717  1.9847292

what: PESTO: Parameter Estimation Optimised, with APSIM Coupling — PESTO-package
title: PESTO: Parameter Estimation Optimised, with APSIM Coupling — PESTO-package
text: High-performance parameter estimation, uncertainty quantification, inverse modelling toolkit built modernised PEST++ algorithms. Provides native R interfaces iterative ensemble smoothers (IES), Gauss-Levenberg-Marquardt (GLM) solvers, global sensitivity analysis, multi-objective optimisation uncertainty. Includes surrogate-accelerated IES via Gaussian Process Random Fourier Features, adaptive SVD backends (randomised SVD, LAPACK, Eigen), convergence-aware adaptive ensemble sizing. Designed large-scale environmental, hydrological, agricultural models support highly-parameterised problems (>100,000 parameters). toolkit model-independent – R function can serve forward model – first-class -process coupling APSIM agricultural-systems model via 'apsimx' package flagship simulator partner.

text: Builds npar x nobs localisation taper directly ensemble, parameter / observation coordinates required. iterative-ensemble-smoother-native localisation Luo & Bhakta (2020): spurious sample correlations parameter observation (artefact finite ensemble size) damped, genuine correlations stand estimated noise floor retained.

title: Correlation-Based Automatic Localisation Taper — correlation_localisation
text: par_diff Matrix (npar x nreal). Parameter anomalies. obs_diff Matrix (nobs x nreal). Observation anomalies. threshold Numeric. Noise floor \(|\rho|\). Negative (default -1) triggers automatic estimation permutation. taper Character. "hard" (indicator) "soft" (linear ramp floor). n_shuffle Integer. Number permutation replicates automatic floor (default 1; replicate yields npar * nobs spurious samples). Ignored threshold >= 0. quantile Numeric (0, 1). Quantile spurious-correlation distribution used floor (default 0.95). Ignored threshold >= 0.

title: Correlation-Based Automatic Localisation Taper — correlation_localisation
text: list rho (npar x nobs taper), threshold (floor used), n_active (count entries non-zero weight), frac_active (count npar * nobs).

title: Correlation-Based Automatic Localisation Taper — correlation_localisation
text: sample correlation \(\rho_{ij}\) parameter-anomaly row \(\) observation-anomaly row \(j\) compared noise floor \(\theta\). threshold < 0 floor estimated destroying parameter-observation link — realisation order observation anomalies randomly permuted, independently per replicate, floor taken high quantile (default 0.95) resulting spurious \(|\rho|\) values. permutation uses R's RNG, estimate reproducible set.seed(). Two tapers offered. "hard" keeps correlations floor unchanged (weight 1) zeroes rest. "soft" applies smooth, monotone ramp \(w_{ij} = \mathrm{clip}((|\rho_{ij}| - \theta) / (1 - \theta), 0, 1)\), downweights near-floor correlations rather thresholding sharply.

title: Correlation-Based Automatic Localisation Taper — correlation_localisation
text: Luo, X. & Bhakta, T. (2020). Automatic adaptive localization ensemble-based history matching. Journal Petroleum Science Engineering, 184, 106559.

title: Correlation-Based Automatic Localisation Taper — correlation_localisation
code: set.seed(1L) npar <- 8L; nobs <- 5L; nreal <- 40L pd <- matrix(rnorm(npar * nreal), npar, nreal) # Make parameter 1 genuinely correlated with observation 1. od <- matrix(rnorm(nobs * nreal), nobs, nreal) od[1L, ] <- od[1L, ] + 2 * pd[1L, ] loc <- correlation_localisation(pd, od) loc$threshold #> [1] 0.2559031 loc$rho[1L, 1L] #> [1] 1

title: Ensemble Solution Kernel (GLM form) — ensemble_solution
text: par_diff Matrix (npar x nreal). Parameter anomalies (deviations mean). obs_diff Matrix (nobs x nreal). Observation anomalies. obs_resid Matrix (nobs x nreal). Observation residuals, simulated minus observed (sim - obs). sign convention required leading negative GLM update (\(\Delta\theta = -\Delta\theta' V s (s^2 + \lambda )^{-1} U^T r\)) yields descent step \(\Phi = \|W(g(\theta) - d^{obs})\|^2\). Passing (obs - sim) inverts gradient causes phi diverge. par_resid Matrix (npar x nreal). Parameter residuals (par - prior mean). weights Numeric vector (nobs). Observation weights (1/sqrt(variance)). parcov_inv Numeric vector (npar). Diagonal inverse parameter covariance. Matrix (npar x nreal-1). Random matrix upgrade_2 (optional). cur_lam Numeric. Current Marquardt lambda. eigthresh Numeric. Eigenvalue truncation threshold (0-1). use_approx Logical. TRUE, skip upgrade_2 (prior-scaling correction). use_prior_scaling Logical. Scale prior covariance. iter Integer. Current iteration number. reg_factor Numeric. Regularisation factor upgrade_2 blending.

title: Ensemble Solution Kernel (GLM form) — ensemble_solution

what: Spectral Spread Effective Sample Size of a Parameter Ensemble — ensemble_spread_ess
title: Spectral Spread Effective Sample Size of a Parameter Ensemble — ensemble_spread_ess
text: Diagnoses ensemble collapse (-dispersion) participation ratio parameter-anomaly covariance eigenspectrum. Given parameter anomalies \(\Delta\Theta\) (deviations ensemble mean, npar x nreal), anomaly covariance \(C = \Delta\Theta \Delta\Theta^{T} / (N - 1)\) eigenvalues \(\lambda_i = s_i^2 / (N - 1)\), \(s_i\) singular values \(\Delta\Theta\).

title: Spectral Spread Effective Sample Size of a Parameter Ensemble — ensemble_spread_ess
text: par_diff Matrix (npar x nreal). Parameter anomalies (deviations ensemble mean). least 2 columns required.

title: Spectral Spread Effective Sample Size of a Parameter Ensemble — ensemble_spread_ess
text: list components ess (spectral spread-ESS), r_max (maximum attainable value \(\min(\mathrm{npar}, N - 1)\)), ess_ratio (ess / r_max, \((0, 1]\)).

title: Spectral Spread Effective Sample Size of a Parameter Ensemble — ensemble_spread_ess
text: spectral spread-ESS participation ratio $$\mathrm{ESS} = \frac{(\sum_i \lambda_i)^2}{\sum_i \lambda_i^2}                    = \frac{(\sum_i s_i^2)^2}{\sum_i s_i^4},$$ effective number directions carrying variance. bounded \([1, r_{\max}]\) \(r_{\max} = \min(\mathrm{npar}, N - 1)\): equal \(r_{\max}\) variance spread isotropically across modes, approaching 1 ensemble collapses onto single direction. ratio invariant global rescaling anomalies, isolates shape collapse (directional degeneracy) magnitude; magnitude tracked separately R-side spread-retention ratio.

title: Spectral Spread Effective Sample Size of a Parameter Ensemble — ensemble_spread_ess
text: Bretherton, C.S., Widmann, M., Dymnikov, V.P., Wallace, J.M. & Blade, . (1999). effective number spatial degrees freedom time-varying field. Journal Climate, 12(7), 1990–2009.

title: Spectral Spread Effective Sample Size of a Parameter Ensemble — ensemble_spread_ess

title: Gaspari-Cohn Localisation Taper — gaspari_cohn
text: Evaluates Gaspari & Cohn (1999) fifth-order piecewise-rational compactly-supported correlation function matrix distances. classical distance-based localisation taper: smooth bump equals 1 zero distance, decays 0 twice localisation radius, identically 0 beyond. Used taper Kalman gain parameters observations carry spatial (otherwise metric) coordinate.

title: Gaspari-Cohn Localisation Taper — gaspari_cohn
text: distances Matrix (npar x nobs). Non-negative parameter-- observation distances. radius Numeric scalar (> 0). Localisation radius \(c\); taper reaches 0 distance \(2c\).

title: Gaspari-Cohn Localisation Taper — gaspari_cohn
text: Matrix (npar x nobs) taper weights \([0, 1]\).

title: Gaspari-Cohn Localisation Taper — gaspari_cohn
text: \(z = d / c\) (distance localisation radius \(c\)): $$G(z) = \begin{cases}   -\tfrac{1}{4}z^5 + \tfrac{1}{2}z^4 + \tfrac{5}{8}z^3 - \tfrac{5}{3}z^2 + 1     & 0 \le z \le 1 \\   \tfrac{1}{12}z^5 - \tfrac{1}{2}z^4 + \tfrac{5}{8}z^3 + \tfrac{5}{3}z^2     - 5z + 4 - \tfrac{2}{3}z^{-1} & 1 < z \le 2 \\   0 & z > 2. \end{cases}$$

title: Gaspari-Cohn Localisation Taper — gaspari_cohn

title: Affine control-variate bias correction across fidelities — mf_control_variate
text: Debiases cheap-fidelity output ensemble sparse expensive sample, per observation dimension. observation j fits first-order autoregressive control variate (linear term Kennedy-O'Hagan multi-fidelity model) high_j ~ a_j + b_j * low_j paired subset, b_j = cov(high_j, low_j) / var(low_j) variance-minimising coefficient, predicts corrected high-fidelity output every realisation a_j + b_j * low_all_j.

text: Wraps user-supplied ODE right-hand side typed pesto_forward_model() whose forward map integrates system fixed time grid reads observation vector resulting state trajectory. generic differential_equations template crop_growth_forward_model() seir_forward_model() specialise; use directly compartmental mechanistic ODE. derivative function derivs signature function(t, y, theta) -> dydt, returning numeric vector length state y. initial state y0 may plain numeric vector (shared across realisations) function function(theta) -> y0 starting condition calibrated (example unknown initial inoculum). observation map observe signature function(traj, theta) -> obs, traj length(times) x length(y0) matrix states integration time (column order matching y0); default reads first state variable every time first. Two integrators available. default solver = "rk4" self-contained classical fourth-order Runge-Kutta n_steps fixed sub-steps successive observation times – external dependency, deterministic, adequate smooth non-stiff systems templates target. solver = "desolve" delegates deSolve::ode() (optional Suggests dependency) method desolve_method, brings adaptive step control stiff solvers ("lsoda", default, switches non-stiff stiff automatically). realisation whose integration fails returns non-finite trajectory reported NA row, pesto_evaluate() pesto_ies_callback() handle failure policy.

title: PESTO Ensemble Manifest (S7 class) — pesto_ensemble_manifest
text: See write_manifest() / read_manifest() YAML serialisation verify_manifest() integrity checking. YAML file authoritative human-readable entry; params, outputs, assimilation context (weights + obs_target) emitted sidecar files whose relative paths recorded inside YAML. Three sidecar modes: format = "rds" (default, verifiable) – RDS . IEEE 754 doubles round-trip bit-exactly; SHA-256 integrity check holds. format = "" (verifiable) – RDS sidecars plus parallel *_inspection.csv files. Hash bound RDS; CSVs decorative. format = "csv_unverified" (verifiable, renamed "csv" PESTO 0.3.2) – CSV-sidecars. Hash recorded recomputed disk (CSV formatter precision loss ~1 ULP). verify_manifest() returns ok = NA + message. Use one-way export non-R analysts; round-trip integrity construction broken. YAML carries explicit integrity: field ("verifiable" / "not_verifiable") derived format downstream non-R tools can branch integrity contract without needing know PESTO-specific format vocabulary.

text: forward_model One : function signature function(theta) -> obs (theta nreal x npar numeric matrix obs nreal x nobs numeric matrix); pesto_forward_model() (typed contract object, e.g. one carrying parallel = "multicore" evaluation strategy); pesto_multifidelity_model() (see fidelity_schedule). bare function auto-wrapped via as_forward_model() call's on_failure. Failed realisations may return rows NA; driver tolerates (see on_failure). run realisations parallel, pass pesto_forward_model built parallel = "multicore" rather bare function. prior_ensemble Matrix data.table, nreal x npar. Columns parameters; optional real_name column preserved present. Column names supply parameter names. warm-start, pass parameter columns previous run's par_ensemble prior next: posterior ensemble valid prior ensemble. obs Named numeric vector. Target observations. obs_sd Numeric scalar vector length nobs. Observation standard deviation(s); IES weights 1/obs_sd. noptmax Integer. Number IES iterations (default 4). lambda Numeric scalar vector. Marquardt lambda per iteration. scalar recycled; vector shorter noptmax right-padded last value (default 1.0). default obs_perturbation = "mda" Marquardt damping ES-MDA inflation (alpha = lambda + 1), supplying lambda fixes inflation schedule must satisfy sum(1 / (lambda + 1)) == 1; , call errors rather returning mis-calibrated posterior. Leave lambda alone use mda_alpha choose schedule natural units. fidelity_schedule Integer vector NULL. consulted forward_model pesto_multifidelity_model(): fidelity level evaluate iteration (recycled / right-padded noptmax). NULL (default) uses highest fidelity every iteration. Ignored otherwise. parcov Numeric vector length npar, diagonal prior parameter covariance. Defaults column-wise variance prior_ensemble; zero negative entries replaced 1.0. eigthresh Numeric. SVD eigenvalue truncation threshold (default 1e-6). use_approx Logical. TRUE (default), skip prior-scaling correction (upgrade_2); matches typical pestpp-ies default. inflation pesto_inflation() specification, NULL (default) covariance inflation. Inflation counteracts ensemble -dispersion – progressive collapse posterior spread finite-ensemble smoother suffers. NULL leaves update identical un-inflated smoother. localisation pesto_localisation() specification, NULL (default) localisation. Localisation tapers Kalman gain suppress spurious finite-sample parameter-observation correlations; active path uses ensemble_solution_localised() (approximate / upgrade_1 form), non-NULL localisation use_approx = FALSE warns drops null-space correction. on_failure Character. "na" (default) carries failed realisations forward unchanged proceeds; "stop" aborts failure. verbose Logical. Print per-iteration phi summaries. phi_tol Numeric scalar NULL. Optional convergence tolerance: non-NULL, iteration stops early relative reduction mean objective function (phi) successive iterations falls phi_tol – phi-reduction stopping rule White (2018). NULL (default) runs full noptmax iterations, leaving update byte-identical unchecked smoother. Use smaller phi_tol demand iterations, larger one stop sooner. Note stopping early truncates ES-MDA schedule, obs_perturbation = "mda" less one likelihood assimilated posterior comes back wide; driver warns happens. obs_perturbation Character, "mda" (default) "none". observations enter update. See Posterior spread observation perturbation. "mda" gives realisation perturbed data vector ensemble-smoother--multiple-data-assimilation scheme, makes returned ensemble posterior sample. "none" assimilates unperturbed vector every realisation: ensemble mean still converges maximum posteriori fit, spread posterior spread must read uncertainty. mda_alpha Numeric vector NULL. ES-MDA inflation schedule \(\alpha_k\), one entry per iteration (recycled / right-padded). NULL (default) uses uniform schedule \(\alpha_k = \)noptmax Emerick & Reynolds (2013). schedule must satisfy \(\sum_k 1/\alpha_k = 1\); Marquardt lambda schedule derived \(\lambda_k = \alpha_k - 1\). meaningful obs_perturbation = "mda". seed Integer NULL. supplied, set.seed(seed) called run (advances session stream exactly direct set.seed() ) value recorded result, as_manifest() carries manifest's seed slot. NULL (default) draws observation noise session stream records NA; reproducibility caller's set.seed().

text: ensemble smoother assimilates , unperturbed observation vector every realisation return posterior sample. Every member feels identical data pull, -member spread prior variance update failed remove, shrink towards right answer ensemble grows. PESTO's default therefore gives realisation \(j\) perturbed data, $$d_j = d + \sqrt{\alpha_k}\,e_j, \qquad e_j \sim N(0, C_D),$$ , iterative smoother assimilates data every step, inflates measurement covariance \(\alpha_k\) subject \(\sum_k 1/\alpha_k = 1\) exactly one likelihood assimilated total. ensemble smoother multiple data assimilation (ES-MDA) Emerick & Reynolds (2013); update step $$m_j \leftarrow m_j + C_{MD}(C_{DD} + \alpha_k C_D)^{-1}       (d + \sqrt{\alpha_k}\,e_j - g(m_j)).$$ PESTO's GLM kernel already computes form: \(C_D = W^{-2}\) Marquardt damping MDA inflation number, \(\alpha_k = \lambda_k + 1\), lambda schedule derived mda_alpha rather set independently. linear-Gaussian problem resulting ensemble covariance matches closed-form conjugate posterior (graded tests/testthat/test-posterior-calibration.R), nominal coverage central intervals realised. reported phi unaffected: always computed unperturbed observations, remains fit data user supplied. obs_perturbation = "none" restores unperturbed update. right choice single best-fit parameter vector wanted spread discarded, wrong choice anything reads ensemble uncertainty.

title: Covariance Inflation Specification for IES — pesto_inflation
text: Four methods offered. "rtps" relaxation--prior-spread (Whitaker & Hamill 2012): parameter's posterior anomalies rescaled \(\alpha(\sigma^{b} - \sigma^{})/\sigma^{} + 1\), \(\sigma^{b}\) \(\sigma^{}\) background (pre-update) analysis (post-update) standard deviations. per-parameter, re-inflates directions collapsed hardest, spectrally-aware workhorse. "adaptive" global, magnitude-targeting scheme: measures mean spread-retention ratio \(q = \mathrm{mean}_j(\sigma^{}_j/\sigma^{b}_j)\) , q falls retention_floor, applies single multiplicative factor \(\min(\texttt{max\_factor}, \texttt{retention\_floor}/q)\) restore lost variance magnitude. "multiplicative" applies fixed factor every iteration. "none" disables inflation. companion diagnostic spectral spread-ESS (ensemble_spread_ess()), recorded iteration regardless method: reports effective number variance-carrying directions detects directional collapse. participation ratio invariant global rescaling, global ("multiplicative" / "adaptive") inflation restores variance magnitude spectral shape; "rtps" method reshapes spectrum. two compose well.

title: Pure-R Reference IES Update — Chen & Oliver (2013) eq. 12 — pesto_reference_ies
code: # Simple linear inverse problem: identify the true theta given noisy obs. set.seed(20260425L) n_par <- 4L; n_obs <- 12L; n_real <- 30L G <- matrix(rnorm(n_obs * n_par) / sqrt(n_par), n_obs, n_par) theta_true <- rnorm(n_par) y_obs <- as.numeric(G %*% theta_true) + rnorm(n_obs, sd = 0.05) weights <- rep(1 / 0.05, n_obs)  par_ens <- matrix(rnorm(n_par * n_real, sd = 1), n_par, n_real) obs_ens <- G %*% par_ens  # One textbook IES upgrade. upg <- pesto_reference_ies(   par_ensemble = par_ens,   obs_ensemble = obs_ens,   obs_target   = y_obs,   weights      = weights,   lambda       = 1.0 ) dim(upg) #> [1]  4 30  # Apply the upgrade and check phi reduces. par_next <- par_ens + upg obs_next <- G %*% par_next Y <- matrix(rep(y_obs, n_real), n_obs, n_real) phi0 <- mean(compute_phi(Y - obs_ens,  weights)) phi1 <- mean(compute_phi(Y - obs_next, weights)) phi1 < phi0 #> [1] TRUE

title: SEIR Compartmental Forward Model — seir_forward_model
text: ready--use ode_forward_model() specialisation classic Susceptible-Exposed-Infectious-Recovered epidemic model closed population (Anderson & May 1991). four states evolve $$\dot S = -\beta S / N,\quad       \dot E = \beta S / N - \sigma E,$$ $$\dot = \sigma E - \gamma ,\quad \dot R = \gamma ,$$ transmission rate \(\beta\), latency rate \(\sigma\) (mean incubation \(1/\sigma\)), recovery rate \(\gamma\) (mean infectious period \(1/\gamma\)). basic reproduction number \(R_0 = \beta / \gamma\).

title: SEIR Compartmental Forward Model — seir_forward_model

title: SEIR Compartmental Forward Model — seir_forward_model
text: times Numeric vector strictly increasing observation times (days), length least two. first entry outbreak start. n_pop Numeric. Total (closed) population size. Default 1000. i0 Numeric. Initial infectious count times[1]. Default 1. Must positive n_pop. solver Character. "rk4" (default) "desolve", ode_forward_model(). n_steps Integer. Fixed RK4 sub-steps observation times (default 10L). ... policy arguments forwarded pesto_forward_model() via ode_forward_model().

title: SEIR Compartmental Forward Model — seir_forward_model
text: pesto_forward_model() S7 object param_names c("beta", "sigma", "gamma") n_obs = length(times) - 1L, emitting infectious prevalence trajectory.

title: SEIR Compartmental Forward Model — seir_forward_model
text: calibration parameters beta, sigma, gamma. population size n_pop initial infectious count i0 fixed structural constants template (outbreak seeded i0 infectious individuals, n_pop - i0 susceptible, nobody exposed recovered). default forward map returns infectious prevalence \((t)\) every time first – compartment case-count series tracks – object calibrates directly observed epidemic curve pesto_ies_callback(). Supply custom observe ode_forward_model() read different compartment (example incidence \(\sigma E\)).

title: SEIR Compartmental Forward Model — seir_forward_model
text: Anderson, R. M. & May, R. M. (1991). Infectious Diseases Humans: Dynamics Control. Oxford University Press.

title: Train a Sparse GP Surrogate via Random Fourier Features — train_rff_surrogate

title: Train a Sparse GP Surrogate via Random Fourier Features — train_rff_surrogate
text: RBF kernel k(x,x') = sigma^2 exp(-||x-x'||^2 / 2l^2) approximated k(x,x') ~ z(x)^T z(x') z(x) = sqrt(2/D) * cos(Wx + b), W random frequencies. w_j ~ N(0, /l^2) b_j ~ Uniform(0, 2pi).

text: Adds two opt-countermeasures finite-ensemble pathologies make iterative ensemble smoother -confident: covariance inflation (-dispersion / ensemble collapse) covariance localisation (spurious finite-sample parameter-observation correlations). default ; NULL specification leaves pesto_ies_callback() pesto_ies_filter() byte-identical previous release.

previous_headings: Covariance inflation and localisation against ensemble collapse
title: PESTO 0.6.0
text: pesto_inflation() – inflation specification four methods: "rtps" (relaxation prior spread, Whitaker & Hamill 2012; per-parameter, spectrally-aware workhorse), "adaptive" (global inflation targeting spread-retention floor), "multiplicative" (fixed factor), "none". pesto_localisation() – localisation specification: "correlation" (automatic, coordinate-free, Luo & Bhakta 2020 – recommended default parameter problems spatial metric) "distance" (classical Gaspari-Cohn taper parameter--observation distance matrix). ensemble_spread_ess() – collapse diagnostic: spectral participation ratio parameter anomaly covariance, .e. effective number variance-carrying directions. Recorded every iteration regardless method. correlation_localisation(), gaspari_cohn(), ensemble_solution_localised() – C++ kernels backing . ensemble_solution_localised() explicit-gain GLM update hosts Schur-product localisation SVD kernel ; taper reproduces ensemble_solution() (approximate form) truncation tolerance.

Note terminology: spectral spread-ESS scale-invariant, used collapse diagnostic, "adaptive" inflation targets variance-magnitude retention floor; "rtps" method reshapes spectrum. title: PESTO 0.5.0
text: pesto_forward_model() — S7 class wrapping forward callable output dimensionality, expected parameter names, failure policy (on_failure, max_fail_frac), evaluation strategy (serial / "multicore" / custom map_fn), fidelity tag. single contract native-callback .pst-file adapter modes honour. pesto_evaluate() — generic runs forward model (multi-fidelity model chosen level) returns shape-guaranteed nreal x nobs matrix "n_failures" / "fail_idx" attributes. as_forward_model() — coerces bare function (passes existing object) contract; used internally bare functions keep working unchanged. pesto_multifidelity_model() — ordered stack fidelity levels (cheapest first) plus relative costs; first-class form bridge’s fidelity vector. mf_control_variate() — affine (Kennedy-O’Hagan AR(1)) control-variate primitive debiases cheap level sparse expensive sample; plug-point surrogate cascades.

title: PESTO 0.5.0
text: New pesto_ies_filter() — filtering counterpart batch smoother pesto_ies_callback(). assimilates time-ordered observation windows one another static parameter ensemble, posterior window becoming prior next, tightening parameter posterior available every window (-season assimilation case). reuses forward-model contract (parallel- multi-fidelity-ready via per-window fidelity_schedule) C++ ensemble_solution() kernel; window_noptmax > 1 gives iterated filter per window. result records per-window history including per-parameter ensemble standard deviation (tightening trace). Filter results (pesto_ies_filter_result) flow manifest contract: as_manifest() tags method = "ies_filter" (added pesto_ensemble_manifest validator) carries fidelity provenance, filtered ensemble first-class scenario downstream consumer.

title: PESTO 0.5.0
text: pesto_ies_callback() gains fidelity_schedule (consulted pesto_multifidelity_model): fidelity level evaluated iteration, supporting cheap-early / expensive-late ramping. final ensemble refresh always uses highest fidelity. Fidelity provenance now closes manifest (C2) lineage: multi-fidelity pesto_ies_callback() run records realised schedule result ($fidelity = list(type, schedule, final_level, n_levels, costs)), as_manifest() inherits pesto_ensemble_manifest fidelity slot unless overridden, write_manifest() / read_manifest() round-trip structured record faithfully (outside integrity hash, affect verify_manifest()). Single-fidelity runs record NULL, manifests unchanged. manifest fidelity slot now documented structured provenance list (legacy named-numeric tags still accepted read). Parallel, fault-tolerant ensemble evaluation: pesto_forward_model parallel = "multicore" dispatches realisations across forked workers via parallel::mclapply() L’Ecuyer streams (reproducible RNGkind("L'Ecuyer-CMRG")); serial bulk evaluation unchanged remains default. apsim_callback() now writes realisation unique per-run file, making closure safe drive parallel (wrap pesto_forward_model(parallel = "multicore")). internal bulk--per-row evaluation helper (.eval_forward_safe) retired favour shared engine behind pesto_evaluate(); -error abort message changed `forward_model` failed forward model failed.

what: Ensemble Manifest as a Portable, Versioned Run Record
title: PESTO 0.3.0
text: New S7 class pesto_ensemble_manifest — versioned, hashed, provenance-tracked container ensemble-run output. Slots cover params, outputs, weights, obs_target, seed, data_hash (SHA-256), fidelity, apsim_version, pesto_version, timestamp, plus method context (method, noptmax, lambda_schedule, failure_rate). documented, versioned format downstream tool can read. New as_manifest() — S7 generic method pesto_ies_callback_result. Non-destructive: wraps without mutating source result. New write_manifest() / read_manifest() — YAML+RDS serialisation. YAML carries metadata + relative paths three sidecar RDS files (*_params.rds, *_outputs.rds, *_assim.rds); RDS used preference CSV IEEE 754 doubles round-trip bit-exactly (SHA-256 integrity check otherwise trip CSV formatter precision loss). New verify_manifest() — recomputes SHA-256 (params, outputs, weights, obs_target, seed) compares stored value, returning diagnostic list. Detects post-write tampering sidecar CSVs. New vignette: ensemble-manifest — end--end demo construct → write → read → verify, plus tamper-detection.

Tolerates per-realisation failures via on_failure = c("na", "stop") reports failure_rate result object. Phase-1 behaviour uses single lambda per iteration (user-supplied schedule); full pestpp-ies-style lambda line-search planned Phase-2 enhancement. Per-realisation template copy, parameter edit via apsimx::edit_apsimx() / edit_apsim(), run, extraction. Failures (edit / run / extractor) surface NA rows IES driver handle. New vignette: apsim-callback — synthetic linear-Gaussian recovery demo plus disabled apsimx example. New benchmark script: inst/benchmarks/d4_callback_vs_pst.R. pesto_ies_callback() records obs_target, obs_sd, weights result list manifest emitter full IES context capture.
